Hands-on with the M5 MacBook Pro: Apple's new chip is a big GPU jump

Published 2026-10-07 18:40 UTC

Apple's new MacBook Pro looks exactly like the old one, so the story is the M5 chip inside. In our early benchmarks the M5's GPU ran about 40 percent faster than the M4 in the same 14-inch chassis, close to Apple's claimed 45 percent, and local AI models generated tokens noticeably faster thanks to the neural accelerators Apple added to each GPU core.

CPU gains are smaller, roughly 12 to 15 percent in multi-core tests. The mini-LED display is brighter outdoors and Thunderbolt 5 is now standard on every configuration, including the base M5 model.

Apple rates the 16-inch MacBook Pro for 24 hours of battery life; we will test that claim in our full review. Prices still start at $1,599 for the 14-inch M5 model, and the laptops ship on October 15.

In our GPU benchmarks, the M5 Max was about 45% faster than the M4 Max in a popular 3D rendering test and around 30% faster in games that support Apple's Metal graphics framework. CPU performance improved more modestly, by about 15% in multi-core tests, which matches Apple's claims for the new chip.

Hardware-accelerated ray tracing has improved noticeably, making the MacBook Pro more capable for 3D artists. Running large language models locally is also faster: a 30-billion-parameter model generated text roughly 1.6 times as fast as on the previous generation, helped by the higher memory bandwidth.

Thermals remain impressive. Under a sustained rendering workload, the 16-inch model's fans became audible after about four minutes but never grew loud, and performance held steady. The 14-inch model with M5 Max ran hotter and throttled slightly after extended use, as earlier generations did.

The improvements matter most for people who do professional graphics or AI work. For most users, the M4 models remain fast, and buyers of older Intel-based MacBook Pros will see a much bigger jump from upgrading. We will publish full battery tests and a final verdict in our complete review next week.
